sentences.text: The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - Insurance Company being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 09.09.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhavnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.295 of 2014.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The brief fact of the present appeal is such that on 30.04.2014, the deceased was going to his place of work on Hero Honda motorcycle No.GJ-4-BM-2834 and when he reached at the place of accident, opponent No.1 rove truck No.GJ-11-U- The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mumtazbanu Wasimkhan Baloch on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146344280/
1 9756 in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/288/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/01/2025 undefined motorcycle of the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result, the accident took place and deceased sustained severe injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
The legal heirs of the deceased have filed aforestated claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-.
The learned Tribunal vide impugned judgment and award dated 09.09.2019 has granted compensation to the tune of Rs.37,71,300/-.
Hence, the present appeal.

3. Learned advocate Mr.Palak Thakkar appearing for the appellant - Insurance Company raise solitary contention in the appeal that learned Tribunal instead of taking average of the last three years income tax returns, relied upon the last income tax return being latest one to compute the loss of dependency and loss of future prospects and thereby learned Tribunal committed serious error in awarding the compensation.
Learned advocate Mr.Thakkar also argued that in total learned Tribunal has granted excess amount of Rs.4,78,550/- by adopting the last income tax return as yardstick to grant compensation.

Learned advocate Mr.Thakkar relied upon judgment of Division Bench of this Court in case of Bhavnaben Shaileshbhai Rank vs. Mahmamkhan Mahmajallauinkhan Pathan, being First Appeal No.3508 of 2021, to argue that the Division Bench of this Court has insisted to take average of the income tax return instead of last year income tax return to be reckoned as yardstick for taking up income of the deceased as it would be apt, appropriate and safe to take average of the income from income tax returns.

entities.text: Bhavnaben Shaileshbhai Rank vs. Mahmamkhan Mahmajallauinkhan Pathan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr.Thakkar would argue that in given circumstances last income tax returns may show lesser abysmally and low income may lead to lower compensation, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/288/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/01/2025 undefined which may lead to injustice.
Therefore, he submitted that safe and proper approach would be to take average of the income, slated in income tax returns.

On the above submissions,
learned advocate Mr.Thakkar submits to allow this appeal.

4. On the other hand, learned advocate Mr.S.D.Panchal would argue that while determining the just and fair compensation, learned Tribunal ought to have taken last income tax return as yardstick for assessing the compensation more particularly when income of the deceased shows rising trend.

He referred to judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sangita Arya and others vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others - 2020 (5) SCC 327, to argue that Hon'ble Supreme Court has deprecated the practice of averaging the income of the deceased / claimant on the basis of three or four previous income tax returns.

entities.text: Sangita Arya and others vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others - 2020 (5) SCC 327
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he submits that learned Tribunal has not committed any error in adopting the last income tax return as statutory evidence for calculating the loss of dependency and loss of future prospects.
Argument is canvassed to dismiss this appeal.

5. Having heard learned advocates for both sides and perusing the evidence on record let first of all refer para 9 of the impugned judgment and award by which learned Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as under :
"9.
Claimant no.1 namely Mumtazbanu Wasmkhan Baloch has filed her affidavit at Exh.32.

is the case of he claimants that deceased Wasimkhan was aged 27 years at the time of accident and by doing brokerage work of land and vehicle and business of scrap from Alang was earning Rs.3,00,000/- p.a. and to prove the income of The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mumtazbanu Wasimkhan Baloch on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146344280/
2

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mumtazbanu Wasimkhan Baloch
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/288/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/01/2025 undefined the deceased the claimants have produced the Income Tax Returns of the deceased at Exh.48, and therefore, this Tribunal is considering the relevant latest Income Tax Return filed by the deceased for the assessment year 2013 -14 which is produced at Exh.48.

On perusal of the said Income Tax Return it transpires that the total income of the claimant for the said year is Rs.2,07,350/- and therefore, the monthly income of the claimant in the year of occurrence of the accident in question can be said to be Rs.17,279/- for just compensation."
6.
The approach of the learned Tribunal in adopting latest income tax return to compute the loss of dependency and future prospects has been questioned by the Insurance Company.
In Rupali Kailas Mamode vs. National Insurance Company Limited - 2023 ACJ 327, the Hon'ble Supreme Court accepted to take up last income tax return as yardstick to award compensation.

entities.text: Rupali Kailas Mamode vs. National Insurance Company Limited - 2023 ACJ 327
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Para 3 of the said judgment reads as under :
"3. The High Court while reducing the compensation has arrived at the conclusion that the income as indicated in the last returns would not be justified and the average of three years is taken and therefore has reduced the compensation.

Though learned counsel for the respondent Insurance Company seeks to contend that the High Court having taken note of the decisions rendered by this Court has arrived at such conclusion, we are of the opinion that in the present facts of the case, in any event such conclusion by the High Court was not justified.

This is for the reason that as noted the deceased was an architect and he was doing contract work, the income-tax returns which he had filed from the period 2004- 2005 onwards indicated that there was a steep increase in his income as compared to a sum of Rs.89,964/- declared in the year 2004-2005 and that benefit cannot be denied.

If this aspect of the matter is kept in perspective, the income was bound to increase many folds if he had survived and such income which is denied to the family is the loss of dependency which was required to be determined."
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/288/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/01/2025 undefined 7.
In Sangita Arya (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court deprecated the approach of the tribunal to take average of the income of the deceased on the basis of ITR filed for last three or four years.

Para 12.2, 13 and 14 thereof reads as under :
"12.2 Second, the High Court determined the income of the deceased by taking the average of the ITRs filed for the years 200203 at Rs. 54,000 p.a., 200304 at Rs.
52,405 p.a., and 200405 at Rs. 51,500 p.a.

The learned Single Judge disregarded the ITR for the year 200607, wherein the income of the deceased was shown as Rs.
98,500 p.a. on the ground that it was allegedly filed almost one year after the death of the deceased.
This finding also is factually incorrect.

sentences.text:
A photocopy of the original ITR for the year 2006- 07 was filed before this Court,
bearing the rubber stamp of the Income Tax Department.
It shows that the date of filing the ITR was 20.04.2007, which is prior to the death of the deceased which occurred on 18.06.2007.
Hence, the High Court was not justified in disregarding the ITR for the year 2006-07 while assessing the income of the deceased.

The Appellants have also placed on record a copy of the ITR for the year 2005-06, which bears the rubber stamp of the Income Tax Department, and reveals the income of the deceased at Rs. 98,100 p.a. during the previous assessment year.
As a consequence, the impugned judgment dated 22.07.2016 passed by the High Court is hereby set aside.

14. On a perusal of the documentary evidence on record i.e. the ITRs for the assessment years 2005-06 and 2006-07, filed prior to the death of the deceased,
which reflect the income of approximately Rs. 1,00,000 p.a. (as assessed by the MACT in its Award dated 22.12.2009), we make this the basis for computing the compensation payable to the Claimants.
We find that the Courts below have not awarded any amount towards future prospects, as mandated by the judgment of the Constitution Bench in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we award future prospects @40% of the income of the deceased."
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/288/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/01/2025 undefined 8.

In earlier judgment in case of Shashikala vs. Gangalakshmamma - 2015 (9) SCC 150, the Hon'ble Apex Court observed that in case of rise of income, last income tax return can be safely relied upon to take base.

Relevant para 20 is reproduced here under :
"20.
The deceased was aged 45 years and was doing transport business.
Though the claimants have filed income tax returns for two assessment years 2005-06 and 2006-07, as per the income tax returns for the year 2006-07, the income of the assessee was Rs.2,02,911/-.

Tribunal did not take the income of the deceased for the assessment year 2006-07 on the ground that only xerox copy was filed and the claimants have failed to examine income-tax authorities to prove the same.
Instead of taking the income of the deceased as per the assessment year 2006-07, the High Court has chosen to calculate the average of the income for two assessment years 2005-06 and 2006-07.
Considering the age of the deceased and the nature of business he was doing, in my considered view, the High Court was not justified in so taking the average of income of the two assessment years.
The deceased was aged 45 years and doing business.
Admittedly, he was also owning agricultural lands.
Even though agricultural income was not shown in the income tax return, it emerges from the evidence that the deceased was also doing agricultural work."

9. Thus, since in case on hand income of the deceased rise and ascend year after year, approach of learned Tribunal to take last income tax return for computing dependency loss and future prospects cannot be faulted.

sentences.text: Since the issue raised by the appellant - Insurance Company is squarely covered by the aforesaid judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the contention put forward by the Insurance Company deserves no merit.

In view of aforesaid NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/288/2020 ORDER DATED:
08/01/2025 undefined judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court, reliance placed by learned advocate Mr.Thakkar on the judgment of Division Bench of this Court would not avail any assistance to the argument of the Insurance Company.

The Division Bench in the judgment in Bhavnaben (supra),
after adopting apprehension that income of victim is declined or stopped or abysmally low, taking of last income tax return would be injurious to grant of just and reasonable compensation.

Thus,
Division Bench advised to take safe and proper course of averaging income.
Thus, finding applies where income of the victim declined and last income tax return show abysmally low income.
But in case where income of the victim rise and ascend year after year, the same would not apply.
11. For the forgoing reasons, the appeal deserves no merit and requires to be rejected.

It is,
accordingly, rejected.

(J. C. DOSHI, J) GAURAV J THAKER The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Mumtazbanu Wasimkhan Baloch on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146344280/
